clock_policy.notes: Gaming card: locked at its no-boost frequency for the run with 'sudo -n nvidia-smi -i <pci> -lgc 2407' (the card then reads 2400 MHz, also at idle) and released with '-rgc' when the run ends, as the 2026-10-01 chain did.

notes: Filled on 2026-10-01 from the machine itself (pip list of each interpreter, nvidia-smi).

One card for every table: PCI 00000000:21:00.0. The two granted cards differ on heavy prefill cells (card 21 holds 2325-2400 MHz where card 22 drops to 2085-2272 MHz), so a run on the spare card 22:00.0 is not comparable and is not offered here.
Every card of this host runs in Exclusive_Process compute mode; the chains left it so, and so does the harness (the preflight probes run with no GPU visible).

Three interpreters, as in /data/bench-runs/fso_release_perf_20261001/5090_stage2/common2.sh: .venv-sgl (fso rows, vLLM, FlashInfer's TRT-LLM CUTLASS MoE, torch-native comparators), .venv-sglang (sglang 0.5.20), .venv-fi (FlashInfer with cuDNN 9.26, which the grouped MXFP8 comparator needs). CUDA_HOME must be exported for the sglang venv: without it deep_gemm's import fails.

Package keys are distribution names: deep_gemm is the sgl-deep-gemm distribution. Every package of the harness's list that an environment has installed is pinned, plus nvidia-cublas and nvidia-cuda-nvrtc, and expecttest where the dense bench's cuBLAS MXFP8 columns import torch.testing._internal.

2026-10-05: no SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR here. Neither apex's config tree (apex-fish-inference cfed1d25) nor sglang 0.5.20's package holds an RTX 5090 Triton MoE config for the two family shapes (E=128,N=768 and E=256,N=512), so the sglang and vLLM Triton comparators run their default tile configs in either case, which is also what apex serves with on this card.
